findings.claim: Change 06 requires successful abrupt-owner recovery in its completed-slice acceptance before change 11 supplies the exclusion mechanism required to permit that recovery.
findings.evidence: Change 06 acceptance says, "Kill the original server, launch a new manager against the same durable backend, list/resume the checkpoint and verify authorized continuation." Its delivery simultaneously says, "A predecessor that may still execute or has uncertain effects remains blocked until trusted exclusion/reconciliation; change 11 supplies abrupt-owner exclusion, so 06 alone does not certify abrupt takeover." Change 11 depends on 06, and the verification contract requires completing and verifying each production slice.
findings.suggested_fix: Make change 06's successful fresh-process continuation test use a predecessor with durably proven orderly exclusion, and require abrupt-loss tests at that stage to demonstrate denial. Move the successful kill-and-takeover acceptance to change 11, where supervisor exclusion is available.

findings.claim: The plan gives contradictory OpenSpec delta instructions for change 12, leaving the replacement of subject-only memory ownership requirements ambiguous.
findings.evidence: The ownership section says, "Change 12 carries the full existing per-user isolation requirement as MODIFIED, preserving every scenario while replacing subject-only memory wording with complete verified owner identity; other additions are ADDED." Change 12 instead specifies "OpenSpec: multi-tenant-isolation, additive requirement ‘Assistant memory is scoped by verified complete owner’," and the emission section requires "at least one additive spec delta" for every change.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the existing requirement to emit under MODIFIED for change 12, preserving its scenarios and updating its ownership language. Distinguish any genuinely additional ADDED requirements, and amend the blanket additive-delta instruction so it does not contradict the required modification.
